messages:
Sam P.: quick one — i want to add a tiny but important tweak to the canary-step schema: include a `quiet_window` and a `min_sample_count` per step so we don't promote on noise. thoughts?
Marta L.: +1 in principle. can you show an example of what you mean? maybe YAML or JSON for the console and API? :eyes:
Sam P.: sure, rough sketch:```json
{
  "steps": [
    { "percent": 5,  "duration": "15m", "quiet_window": "5m", "min_sample_count": 500, "guards": { "error_rate_delta_pct": 150, "p95_ms_increase_pct": 30 } },
    { "percent": 25, "duration": "30m", "quiet_window": "10m", "min_sample_count": 2000 }
  ],
  "fallback_policy": "instant-rollback"
}```
Ryan C.: i like the intent. 2 quick things: 1) min_sample_count should be configurable as requests or tokens? for embeddings we should probably use requests; for generation maybe tokens. 2) quiet_window should be required for every step (helps baseline delta calculation)
Jen K.: watch out for bursty workloads — you can hit min_sample_count quickly in a spike but the sample won't be representative. recommend combining min_sample_count with a `min_duration` and a `stability_window` metric that checks variance in p95 across the quiet_window :warning:
Anya S.: for console UX we can show an estimated time-to-sample based on recent traffic so users know when a step will actually complete. show both time and expected samples. small widget: "estimated 18m to reach 2k reqs"
Sam P.: good call. so schema fields: percent, duration (max), min_duration (optional), quiet_window, min_sample_count, sample_unit (requests|tokens), guards (error_delta_pct, latency_pct, cost_pct), abort_on_guard:boolean. also add `weight_based` vs `rps_based` targeting modes.
devops-bot: automated-check: schema-proposal-lint passed; flagged: missing docs for `stability_window` and `sample_unit` default.
Marta L.: about guard thresholds: error_rate_delta_pct 150 means 1.5x baseline, correct? we should standardize units (absolute vs relative) and default to relative pct. also, tie rollback to signal strength: require both error_rate and p95 to breach for >2 consecutive quiet_windows before auto-rollback.
Ryan C.: agree on two-signal rule. also, prefer `percent_of_traffic` be implemented as weight on routed cohorts rather than strict RPS split — avoids artifact when autoscaling kicks in. but we need an escape hatch: ability to target by `cohort_ratio` or `fixed_rps` for low-traffic customers.
Jen K.: operational note: add a mandatory telemetry hook name that we can use to attach evals/e2e tests at each step (e.g., `canary_eval_set: critical_prompts_v1`). prevents silent regressions in quality that pure latency/error guards miss.
Sam P.: ok, next actions captured: 1) i'll update schema draft with fields above and add examples for generation vs embedding workloads. 2) ryan will draft semantics for weight_vs_rps targeting and the console will show ETA using recent 1h traffic. 3) jen will write recommended stability checks and suggested default thresholds. 4) anya will mock the ETA widget + step status UI.
Marta L.: timeline? can we get a first-pass API wire by EOD Friday so product can review? :rocket:
Ryan C.: i can do semantics doc by Thursday. jen can you take lead on defaults?
Jen K.: will take defaults + a short runbook for interpreting non-actionable blips.
Sam P.: thanks — i'll open the PR and put the schema file under `api/v1/canary-schema.json` and ping this thread. adding `quiet-window` naming to be backwards-compatible with existing `hold_period` concept.
Anya S.: i'll mock on Friday AM and post screenshots.
devops-bot: reminder: link to rollout-telemetry-dashboard needs to be added to schema docs (ticket #RI-908).
Marta L.: perfect. if we can make the defaults conservative and visible in the UI, this will reduce accidental rapid promotions. :thumbsup:
